questionAnswers.question: Which lifecycle point allocates each identity?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6 law 6; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §2 'Lifecycle consequences' 1-4 and §3.1; resolved-inputs.v2#planIdContract

answer.RequestId (REQUEST-ID-V1): Host-minted at TRUSTED INGRESS, allocated and atomically reserved before parsing, lookup or event creation. Correlation metadata only; excluded from every semantic identity and outcome. Carried across host components by the opaque, non-copyable, non-serializable TrustedRequestContextV3, whose independently rooted host authority — not the context, not any module-global helper — owns the reservation-to-object registry.
answer.ProjectId (PROJECT-ID-V1): At REQUEST VALIDATION: host verifies or host-allocates it from the exact no-follow .opensip/project-id.v1 marker plus host registry. A persisted CSPRNG allocation never derived from mutable state; callers cannot supply it.
answer.ExecutionId: At ATTEMPT ADMISSION. (Freeze §6's ExecutionId allocation sentence is a verbatim content anchor of check-retention-custody-v23/v24.py.) Injected into the core, never affects the evidence digest, excluded from Plan/evidence semantics.
answer.SnapshotId (SNAPSHOT-ID-V1): At SNAPSHOT BINDING, after attempt admission: constructed and verified from the closed snapshot descriptor and sealed file/link bytes.
answer.PlanId (PLAN-ID-V1): Immediately after snapshot binding: the closed 13-field PlanDescriptorV1 is constructed and PLAN-ID-V1 verified by exact CVE1 framing and SHA-256, before cache lookup, provider dispatch or stage execution. Supplied IDs are never authority (suppliedAuthority: false).
answer.RunId: ALLOCATION POINT is stated — the host, on seal (blueprint §3.1: 'final RunId allocation on seal'). The DERIVATION is not: operability.v10.json states verbatim 'No exact RunId derivation recipe is binding yet.' (verified on the live bytes). Freeze §6 law 6's 'Recipe status' paragraph withdraws the earlier assertion that all four keep separate recipes.
answer.evidence identity / EvidenceDigest: Host-owned, at evidence assembly and seal. No binding byte recipe — freeze §7.1 row 3; operability.v10#requestIdContract.fixtures[8].parked.

questionAnswers.caveat: Answerable in full for allocation POINTS. Two of the seven (RunId, evidence identity) have an allocation point and no derivation recipe, and the package says so explicitly rather than leaving it to be discovered.

questionAnswers.question: Which component may read the worktree, spawn a provider, write durable state, seal a Run, derive policy, and exit the process?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6 laws 5, 8, 13; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §3.1, §4 workspace table, §2 consequences 7-9; v1-slice.md §5 laws 4-5 and §2.4
questionAnswers.answer: NO SINGLE COMPONENT MAY DO ALL SIX — the question is a decomposition test and the package answers it cleanly. (1) The ORCHESTRATION HOST (crates/host) reads the worktree, spawns and supervises providers, writes durable state through the sole host-owned durable-state authority, seals the Run, and derives the D9 HostTermination. (2) POLICY IS DERIVED IN THE PURE CORE (crates/core): freeze §6 law 5 — the core receives sealed data, exposes no effectful callback or port, mints no entropy, and returns CoreCompletion INCLUDING policyOutcome; v1-slice §2.4 'Evaluate policy in the same pure core'. crates/policy must not own exit mapping, persistence or provider access. (3) PROCESS EXIT is the BINARY's: freeze §6 law 13 — 'one binary site performs process exit'; blueprint §4 gives bins/opensip 'the only numeric-exit write site'. The host finalizer constructs HostTermination; the binary writes the code.
questionAnswers.caveat: crates/store is an implementation of the host's single durable-state authority, not a peer authority (blueprint §3.1). Inventing a second store authority is a freeze §8 failure condition.

questionAnswers.question: How does CI handle layer 4?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §5 (disposition row + the layer definition added 2026-08-04) and §6 law 2; product-dispositions.v1.json $.decisions.A1-RI-04; resolved-inputs.v2#configuration.precedence; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §1, §7.2 step 3, §7.3
questionAnswers.answer: Layer 4 is the UNTRACKED, MACHINE-LOCAL OVERRIDE file — one of six configuration precedence layers (1 compiled defaults, 2 user-global, 3 tracked project intent, 4 untracked local override, 5 allowlisted environment, 6 command flags). CI and every non-interactive invocation DOES NOT LOAD OR RESOLVE IT. Verified live in the binding packet: product-dispositions.v1.json $.decisions.A1-RI-04.rule — 'The CI/non-interactive profile does not load or resolve layer-4 analysis-affecting untracked overrides. Their presence is not an admission failure. Local interactive runs may use layer 4 only when its values and provenance enter PlanId and the explain projection.' The obligation is NOT-LOADED, so mere presence neither changes PlanId nor rejects admission; blueprint §7.3's minimum integration golden requires CI to derive the same result whether the file is absent or present. resolved-inputs.v2#planIdContract.fieldCanonicalization.resolvedConfiguration adds that under ci a layer-4 record is invalid.
questionAnswers.caveat: See defect D-7: v1-slice.md §6 (authority level 2) still presents this as an OPEN decision with a two-branch provisional posture. The binding packet outranks it under §1/§2 authority order, so I was not forced to choose — but the inconsistency is unrecorded.

questionAnswers.question: Why is syntax not globally weaker than semantics?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6 law 3, read there in full as §8 instructs; corroborating sites it names: IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §4 (crates/facts) and §7.3; freeze §6 law 4; v1-slice.md §5 law 3 and §2.3
questionAnswers.answer: Because C-1 is PREDICATE-RELATIVE and there is no global fact or layer ordering, so there is no rank to compare and therefore nothing to fall back DOWN to. Strength is a property of a PREDICATE and its Coverage, not of a tier: a syntactic fact that exactly satisfies what a predicate requires is sufficient FOR THAT PREDICATE, and a semantic fact that does not is not. Law 4 is the other half — unmet requiredness becomes a typed deficiency, never a pass and never a false no-match — so substituting a syntactic fact for an unavailable semantic one would convert an unmet requirement into an apparent pass, which law 4 forbids outright. Law 3 states the implementer's own framing of the question ('why may I not just degrade to the syntactic answer?') and answers it: because the ordering it presumes does not exist, and because the substitution it licenses is a false negative wearing a green result. The corroborating sites are named and both check out: blueprint §4 forbids crates/facts a 'global fact-tier rank' and crates/graph a 'global origin/fact rank'; blueprint §7.3's required-provider-outage golden demands typed Coverage deficiency, policy indeterminate and D9 indeterminate with 'no silent syntax substitution'.
questionAnswers.caveat: Read as one continuous passage in §6 law 3, exactly as §8 says. It did not need reassembling from fragments.

questionAnswers.question: What does a provider-unavailable predicate do?
questionAnswers.answer: A VALID provider 'Unavailable' — and a deterministic 'BudgetExhausted' — is an EXACT COVERAGE OUTCOME, not a fault. It yields a typed Coverage deficiency; the required predicate is unsatisfied; policy returns INDETERMINATE; the Run is still sealed COHERENTLY; and D9 terminates INDETERMINATE (exit 3, confirmed against the executed oracle's classToExitCode). There is NO silent syntax substitution — that is law 3/law 4 (see Q4). The neighbouring cases are deliberately different: a malformed/partial protocol, crash, identity mismatch or bad exit is a D9 provider-protocol FAULT (faultCause=provider-protocol, errorCode=PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION); a promised-but-missing or unspawnable signed profile artifact is DELIVERY-REQUIRED. An incomplete semantic universe 'cannot produce PlanId and instead produces Coverage provider-unavailable' (resolved-inputs.v2, verbatim), i.e. the failure lands before provider execution.
questionAnswers.caveat: Freeze §3's FACT-PLANE row lists as blocking work 'declare the sufficiency view type and the rungUnavailableBecause vocabulary' — so the deficiency VOCABULARY is not fully closed even though the behaviour is.

questionAnswers.question: How does an exact graph accelerator differ from a semantic graph producer, and what happens when the accelerator is absent, corrupt, partial, or stale?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6 law 8; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §2.1 rules 1-8 and §7.4 gate table; §4 (crates/index vs crates/graph)

answer.distinction: An EXACT ACCELERATOR is project-scoped, rebuildable, OPTIONAL, and must be PARITY-EQUIVALENT to canonical traversal; it is host-side cache work and can change no answer. A SEMANTIC PRODUCER is any graph computation whose algorithm, version, parameters, thresholds, approximation or inputs CAN change an edge, finding, ordering, omission or Coverage — it is not a cache, and must follow normal Plan/fact/provenance/Coverage/evidence custody and provider identity. It may never be hidden behind crates/index.
answer.absent: Bypassed. Deleting the entire cache must preserve second-process inspection and canonical reference answers (§7.4 'absence'). GraphView reference traversal is the correctness oracle, not a slow degraded mode.
answer.corrupt: Detected before use and bypassed or rebuilt. Every required component is digest/count/schema/kind/version/parameter checked before the single atomic active-pointer transition. Cache corruption may never become a false empty or clean result (law 8).
answer.partial: UNREPRESENTABLE. Generations run building -> complete -> active -> stale -> collectible; queries pin exactly one generation; 'partial or cross-generation answers are unrepresentable'. A query concurrent with activation sees exactly its pinned old or new complete generation, never a splice.
answer.stale: Stale Snapshot / fact-view / project inputs cannot hit; the required lookup dimensions are ProjectId, Snapshot, exact fact view/partition set, graph schema, index kind, implementation version and parameters. Stale collection waits for the pin to drain.
answer.boundFailure: If the canonical computation cannot meet a declared bound the result is explicit Coverage/indeterminate — never an empty edge set or a clean verdict.

questionAnswers.caveat: Blueprint §2.1 rule 4 states explicitly that the lookup-dimension list prevents unsafe reuse but does NOT define the parked FactViewId or the cache/regeneration key byte recipe — those are §7.1 escalations (rows 5 and 6).

questionAnswers.question: Which process contains rustc_driver, how is it identified, and why is it not a sandbox?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §3.3, §4 (bins/rust-provider, crates/facts-rust), §1.1 note N-2; IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6 law 10 and §3.2 item 5; v1-slice.md §2.1 and §4

answer.whichProcess: bins/rust-provider (opensip-rust-provider) — the bundled sidecar. ONE supervised process per Rust SEMANTIC UNIVERSE. It is explicitly NOT linked into the host: crates/facts-rust must not own 'rustc_driver linked into the host', and the provider must not import host/core/store.
answer.howIdentified: By the required identity handshake over the RUST-PROVIDER-PROTOCOL wire contract — rust-provider-protocol.v2.json MERGED with the v4 overlay per note N-2, NOT delivery.v2. Protocol major is 2, and I verified the whole precedence chain by direct lookup rather than trusting the prose: rust-provider-protocol.v2#protocolIdentity.protocolMajor == 2 (a real JSON int); protocolIdentity IS in v4's inheritedTopLevelSelectors and is NOT among the eight replacedSelectors; delivery.v2#rustSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.major == 1 and that value LOSES. (delivery.v2's TypeScript major is also 1, and that one is correct for the Node worker.) Identity is further pinned by the rust-v1 semantic universe key — rustCommitHash, rustcVersion, cargoVersion, hostTriple, targetTriple, sysrootDigest, provider build and artifact digests — all of which enter PlanId, with no system rustc, Cargo, sysroot or PATH lookup permitted to substitute.
answer.whyNotASandbox: Because the provider and compiler are TCB-ACCEPTED. Freeze §6 law 10: 'one supervised, pinned compiler process per semantic universe. It is TCB/fault containment, not a sandbox.' Blueprint §3.3: 'fault containment and compiler-instability containment. It is not a sandbox... the product must not claim capability confinement.' v1-slice §4 EXCLUDES from v1 any 'claims that a process boundary, Rust sidecar, narrow interface, signature, or stage label provides runtime capability confinement', and §5 law 9: 'labels are not confinement'. Real confinement is blocked on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT, which freeze §7 records as PARKED with every dependent feature excluded.

questionAnswers.question: How do you obtain the D9 axes-to-class derivation, and why is executing the pinned checker's verified closure compliant while transcribing a predecessor contract is not?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §2 rule 5, §7.3; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §1.1 rule 5 and note N-5, §5 D9 row, §7.2 step 1
questionAnswers.answer: YOU RUN THE PINNED CHECKER. d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json does not state the total axes-to-class function; its referenceDerivation names check-d9-v1.14.py::check+derive_class+derive_codes+reduce_concurrent+V17.V16.derive_class, and that checker is inside the freeze payload (§2). The sole admitted invocation is 'python3 -I -B'. WHY EXECUTING IS COMPLIANT: freeze §2 rule 5 and §7.3 — a retained checker that hash-verifies a file set before executing it, and whose independent review covered that set, may internally execute superseded or REJECTED predecessors; those files are RUNTIME INPUTS OF THE INSTRUMENT, they acquire no normative standing, and the verdict covers the closure it verified. WHY TRANSCRIBING IS NOT: rules 3 and 4 scope the CONTRACT YOU IMPLEMENT — a REJECTED version is not normative and a superseded version is not a fallback — so copying check-d9-v1.10.py's derive_class body (where the implementation actually lives, five delegation levels down) into Rust would be implementing bytes that carry no verdict. The distinction is between obtaining a VALUE from a verified instrument and adopting BYTES as a contract.

questionAnswers.question: What retained objects establish a no-match and a verdict after Phase 1A?
questionAnswers.answerableAs: CORRECTLY-SIGNPOSTED BLOCKER — the package tells me plainly that this does not exist yet, rather than letting me discover it.
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §3.1, §3 EVIDENCE row, §3 evaluation-proof candidate row, §7.1; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §1.1 notes N-3 and N-4, §5 EVIDENCE and V10 rows, §7.2 steps 6-7
questionAnswers.answer: THE PACKAGE DOES NOT TELL ME, AND SAYS SO. This is exactly freeze §3.1's mandatory Phase-1A insertion — 'exact evaluation-proof model for match, no-match, indeterminate/error, and verdict claims' plus 'exact retained objects for independent verification or regeneration' — and that insertion has not happened. What I CAN establish from the permitted set: (a) the six-shape proofObligationsByClaimShape map (local-match, relationship-match, aggregate-match, NO-MATCH, indeterminate, error) lives in evaluation-proof.v8, which freeze §3 records as still the V10 item-1 artifact and which is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with a companion checker carrying a standing defect record — 'EVALUATION-PROOF is therefore not seal-ready'; (b) the v10..v13 chain carries ZERO occurrences of 'no-match' and repairs a different thing; (c) evidence.v10 defines no EvidenceBundle, no EvaluationEvidence, no SubjectSetCommitment, no outcomeSetDigest and no subject-set Merkle framing at all, and imports universeCommitment and outcomeSetCommitment by equality from an unapplied vector. So the shape exists only in unapplied candidates and blueprint note N-4 forbids implementing from them. The honest answer is: the retained-object set is the Phase-1A packet, and it does not exist.
questionAnswers.gradedAs: Not a package defect. The package is consistent, explicit and correctly blocking here. It is the single largest thing standing between this package and a buildable milestone.

questionAnswers.question: What happens after proof expiry/purge without rewriting the sealed Run?
questionAnswers.answerable: PARTIALLY — the semantics are described; they are not implementable
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §4.6, §3.1, §5 CD-RT-5 row, §7 (A1-RTV4-02); IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §1.1 note N-4, §3.4, §7.2 step 7
questionAnswers.answer: DESCRIBED: the sealed Run is never rewritten. What changes is EFFECTIVE CAPABILITY — a demotion with unit-granular reasons, computed so that the seal enters only as a CEILING (freeze §4.6 records the independent verification of P4 in its strong form, result == min(sealed, best) at all 276 cases) and so that purge can never RAISE capability (40,000 randomised multi-position trials, zero counterexamples). Read-time unavailability after purge publishes D9 'indeterminate' / exit 3 with an EMPTY reason-code list — derived, not chosen, because 0 of 9 deficiency members, 0 of 9 reason codes and 0 of 19 error codes name retention-driven read-time unavailability. That class-with-no-remedy is a real defect owned by D9, published as RT23-B-RES-01. Purge is a journaled state machine that renames projects/<ProjectId> into quarantine/ and resumes from exact durable state (blueprint §3.4). NOT IMPLEMENTABLE: the derivation lives in retention-tiers.v23 Part B, carried byte-identically into retention-tiers.v24, which is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, is NOT the §3.1 insertion, and selects no retention default (durableDefault remains UNSELECTED). Blueprint note N-4: 'Do not implement a retention default, proof, degradation record, or purge transition from any of them.' CD-RT-5 is BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A — verified live in product-dispositions.v1.json $.pendingDecisions.CD-RT-5.status.
questionAnswers.caveat: Freeze §4.6 records V10 item 3 as DISCHARGED. That is a statement about an architecture obligation, not a licence to build: the artifact carrying the discharge binds nothing.

questionAnswers.question: Which crate owns every binding contract and first golden?
questionAnswers.source: IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §4 (initial Rust workspace map, ownership + forbidden imports + dependency direction) and §5 (contract -> module/type/test map, with a 'Conformance entry point' column)
questionAnswers.answer: §5 gives, for each binding surface, a first Rust owner, a first API/type and a conformance entry point; §4 gives the crate boundaries, the forbidden import edges (which are 'conformance tests from the first commit') and the expected dependency direction. Ownership resolves for every surface: D9 -> host::finalize + types::termination + the binary exit site; C-2 -> plan::{intent,execution} + host::admission; FACT-PLANE -> facts::{relation,coverage,sufficiency}; RESOLVED-INPUTS -> host::{resolve,snapshot} + plan::identity; FACT-IDENTITY -> facts::identity; R-1 -> core + host::orchestrate; EVIDENCE -> crates/evidence (shape only); V10/retention -> blocked; VERSIONING -> crates/versioning; DELIVERY -> crates/delivery + both provider adapters; RUST-PROVIDER-PROTOCOL -> provider-protocol + facts-rust + bins/rust-provider + host::finalize; OPERABILITY -> host::{ingress,events,projection,audit} + store; TRUSTED-REQUEST-CONTEXT -> host::ingress + types; TM -> host storage/read-set/config/temp/projection policies; PRODUCT -> composition/profile/admission policy.
questionAnswers.caveat: Two §1.1 rows have no §5 row: CLAIMS (claim-register.v1.json — a status register, not a surface, correctly excluded) and evaluation-proof.v13 (folded into the V10 row and, per freeze §3, not a registered surface at all). Blueprint §5 also warns in its own words that the 'First API / type' column is proposed Rust naming rather than artifact strings, and that where the column and the artifact disagree the artifact wins.

questionAnswers.question: Which apparent features must reject rather than be stubbed?
questionAnswers.source: v1-slice.md §4 and §2.2 and §5 law 9; IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §4.2 and §3.2 joins 2-3; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §5.A, §7.3, §8.2, §9

mustRejectAtAdmission: Probe stages, simulation, and every scenario-effectful mode (ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT is PARKED)
Third-party or untrusted imperative rules; untrusted native or WASM contributions
External-scanner fact derivation — EVEN WHEN VALID UNDER THE GENERAL C-2 SCHEMA (this is the trap: schema-valid is not admissible)
Any claim that a process boundary, Rust sidecar, narrow interface, signature or stage label provides runtime capability confinement
A resident host, daemon autostart, resident-default UX, or multi-project residency
Public extension marketplace, public in-process plugin ABI, third-party lifecycle parity
Full MCP/agent-protocol parity, Cloud-required analysis/verdict/evidence paths, model calls anywhere on the analysis path
Repair/mutation workflows, broad command-surface parity, a columnar/vector engine as day-one
answer.typedOutcomes: Capability-runtime-dependent forms retain domain reason FEATURE.REQUIRES_CAPABILITY_RUNTIME; a C-2-valid but v1-excluded external scanner retains FEATURE.EXTERNAL_SCANNER_NOT_IN_V1. BOTH map to D9 rejectionCause=extension-admission-rejected and public errorCode=EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED. Domain detail and D9 codes are not interchangeable vocabularies and an implementation may invent neither.
answer.whereItRejects: During REQUEST VALIDATION, from the committed PlanIntent, BEFORE attempt admission — creating no ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId, ExecutionPlan or Run. Post-admission substitution is also rejected before any stage executes, and is a host defect rather than a second admission path.
answer.theStubbingProhibition: Freeze §4.2: 'An excluded form must reject at admission. Hiding one behind a flag still admits it and violates the slice.' Blueprint §9: 'A feature flag that admits an excluded form is still admission and is prohibited.'

determinabilityOfNormativeBytes.question: The brief asks whether the package makes it determinable which bytes to build against, reading the DISPOSITION column rather than the verdict column.
determinabilityOfNormativeBytes.answer: YES, DETERMINABLE — but on a stale rationale.
determinabilityOfNormativeBytes.reasoning: The rule is mechanical and I applied it: the normative bytes are blueprint §1.1's filename+SHA-256 pins; a link without a digest is a pointer; a version whose independent review is REJECTED is not normative and its predecessors are not a fallback; nothing promotes an unnamed higher version. So I would build the §1.1 heads, and I verified all of them recompute correctly. Reading the DISPOSITION column as instructed: EVIDENCE and TM are 'UNSET — BLOCKS FREEZE', so their shapes are portable and their surfaces are not settled — blueprint §5.1's E-NS-1 correctly narrows TM to 'ProjectId half buildable, root half not'. WHAT IS NOT DETERMINABLE is why those heads are the right ones: §9.1's stated reason for holding four reviewed-passing successors out is falsified by §7.8 of the same document and by three green companion instruments on disk (D-1). An implementer can determine WHICH bytes; they cannot determine whether the package still means it.
determinabilityOfNormativeBytes.secondRuleThreeTension: Freeze §2 rule 3 forbids implementing a version whose independent review is REJECTED. PC-7 fires on TWO artifacts. For rust-provider-protocol.v2 the package resolves the tension explicitly and well (§3.2 item 5: what is normative is the MERGE, and not one of the 18 inherited selectors was ever a blocking surface). For threat-model.v3 there is NO equivalent resolution recorded — the REJECT is scoped to $.storageNamespace and the scoping is done implicitly, in blueprint §1.1's row and §5.1's E-NS-1, while rule 3 is written as a whole-version rule. Recording a §3.2-style resolution for TM would close the second half of a rule the package has already closed the first half of.

None of the six §8 package-failure conditions was hit. I was not forced to choose retention, invent a second store authority, decide the core effect boundary, select a Rust substrate, choose layer-4 CI behaviour, create an exit mapping, or decide which version of a binding artifact is normative.
Which bytes to build against IS determinable: the §2 version-selection rule is mechanical, blueprint §1.1 carries the pins, and every pin I recomputed matched.

The package's two hardest instructions both worked in practice. The D9 derivation was obtained by EXECUTING the pinned oracle and rederived 45 of 45 goldens plus the branch the JSON leaves implicit. And §7.1's park property made two UNLISTED digest gaps escalable without an amendment.

Where the package blocks, it blocks EXPLICITLY and in advance. Blueprint §5.1 predicted both week-one walls precisely, including the trap that a green PLAN-ID-V1 vector suite proves nothing about field 3 — and it was right in both cases, including the exact placeholder literals.
verdictReasons.passIsNotSufficiency: A PASS here means the package is answerable and forces no forbidden choice. It does NOT mean the milestone is buildable: four of blueprint §9's seven week-one items run into a named wall, and two of them stopped this run cold. It does not close R2-FINAL-03 and could not have.
verdictReasons.againstThePass: Ten defects are recorded, three graded HIGH. The sharpest is D-1: freeze §9.1's stated reason for withholding four reviewed-passing successors is false on the live tree and is contradicted by §7.8 of the same document — and the two successors withheld are exactly the two that would close the two gaps that stopped this litmus.

singleMostValuableRepair: Re-run §9.1's PC-5 paragraph against the live tree and act on what it says. Its own release condition — 'until each successor has a companion instrument and the head moves as a deliberate act' — is already satisfied for three of the four (check-c2-v11.py, check-delivery-v4.py and check-r1-v1.6.py all exist and all exit 0, and freeze §7.8 records that they were written). Deciding those head moves deliberately would, in one act, unblock BOTH week-one identity items that stopped this run, remove the largest gap between what the package says and what is on disk, and let the next implementer get past §7.2 step 3. Everything else in this report is smaller than that.
